description: Draw Nassi-Shneiderman diagrams (structograms), run them step by step and turn them into code – and back: Python, Java, C, C++, C#, JavaScript/TypeScript, Kotlin and Rust. Structorizer compatible (.nsd, full command set incl. Turtleizer), optionally with the original Structorizer (16 target languages). Export as SVG, PNG, JSON, XML and AI pseudocode.
cmd.exportSingle: Save Diagrams as Separate Structorizer Files...
config.trueLabel: Label of the true branch of an alternative (e.g. true, yes, T). Empty = true.
config.falseLabel: Label of the false branch of an alternative (e.g. false, no, F). Empty = false.
config.prettyOperators: Show operators nicely in the diagram (!= as ≠, <= as ≤, >= as ≥; old notation <- as ←).
config.theme: Color theme of the structogram in the editor and in the preview.
config.theme.enum0: Like VS Code: dark diagram with a dark color theme, otherwise light
config.exportTheme: Color theme when exporting as SVG or PNG image.
config.exportTheme.enum2: Always light (white background, good for printing)
config.highlightKeywords: Color keywords (INPUT, OUTPUT, var, for, while, and ...), function calls, data types, strings and assignment, comparison and arithmetic operators in the diagram.
config.defaultTargetLanguage: Target language for “Generate Code from Structogram”. Empty = ask every time. Built-in translation: python, java, c, cpp, csharp, javascript, kotlin, rust. Original Structorizer: structorizer:Python, structorizer:Java, structorizer:Basic ... (generator name).
config.importEngine: Which parser “Create Structogram from Code” uses for C and Java files.
config.importEngine.enum0: Built-in parser (fast, no Java, also handles Python, C++, C#, JavaScript, TypeScript, Kotlin, Rust)
config.importEngine.enum1: Original Structorizer parser for C and Java files (COBOL/Processing always use it)
config.structorizer.jarPath: Path to Structorizer.jar or the Structorizer folder. Empty = use the automatically downloaded version.
config.structorizer.javaPath: Java program (version 11 or newer) used to start Structorizer.
config.structorizer.exportOptions: Additional switches for the Structorizer export, e.g. "-b" (braces on their own line), "-c" (instructions as comments), "-t" (no translation).
cmd.toggleExecutionLocation: Show Execution in Editor or Panel
config.executionPanelLocation: Where the execution (console, input, Turtleizer, variables) is shown: below the diagram in the structogram editor or in the panel at the bottom of VS Code, next to *Problems*, *Output* and *Debug Console*. Can be switched live, also with the command *Struktograf: Show Execution in Editor or Panel* or the buttons in the editor and the panel.
config.executionPanelLocation.enum0: Below the diagram in the structogram editor
config.executionPanelLocation.enum1: In the panel at the bottom of VS Code (next to Problems, Output, Debug Console)
cmd.toggleToolbarLocation: Show Tools in Editor or Sidebar
config.toolbarLocation: Where the structogram tools are shown: in the toolbar at the top of the editor or in the *Struktograf* view in the activity bar (like the Explorer). Can be switched live, also with the command *Struktograf: Show Tools in Editor or Sidebar* or the button in the editor title bar.
config.toolbarLocation.enum0: Toolbar at the top of the structogram editor
config.toolbarLocation.enum1: Struktograf view in the activity bar (like the Explorer)
debugger.label: ▶ Run Structogram (Struktograf)
debugger.program: Structogram file (.nsd) to run. Default: the open structogram.
debugger.stopOnEntry: Pause at the first element (like F10) instead of running.
welcome.debug:
The active structogram can be run directly:
[Debug Structogram](command:struktogramm.debug)
[Run Without Debugging](command:struktogramm.runNoDebug)
Breakpoints: F9 in the structogram. The debugger list does not recognize the structogram editor – inside the editor, F5 starts it directly.
config.checks: Checks in the structogram: **errors** (red, “!”) for things that do not work – e.g. syntax errors, a variable without a value, an unknown function, `leave` outside a loop, assignment with = instead of := – and **hints** (yellow, “i”, each with a reason) for deviations from good practice or common conventions – e.g. a variable without a type, an input without a prompt, a case selection on a condition, a possible endless loop, a value that is never used. Which hints appear is set per group in the *Hints* settings (good practice, conventions, misleading, possible logic errors). Messages appear as a badge on the element (tooltip on hover) and in the *Problems* view.
config.hints.bestPractice: Show **good practice** hints (yellow): variable, constant, parameter or return value without a type, subroutine without a return value lacking `: void`, input without a prompt, variable only declared in another branch. Errors are always shown.
config.hints.conventions: Show **conventions** hints (yellow): case selection on a condition, conditions as case labels, several statements in one block, empty loop body, empty block, structogram without a name. Common conventions from teaching and practice – DIN 66261 only defines the symbols, not such rules.
config.hints.confusion: Show **misleading** hints (yellow) – works, but invites mistakes: “else” branch labeled with a condition, variable sometimes text and sometimes a number, decimal numbers compared with `=`, value never used.
config.hints.logic: Show **possible logic error** hints (yellow): endless loop without exit, loop condition never changes, unreachable element, decimal number divided by 0 (gives Infinity).
config.hints.codegen: Show **code generation** hints (yellow): commands that cannot be translated into one or all target languages (turtle commands, growing arrays …).
config.language: Language of Struktograf: editor, tools, execution, check messages and comments in generated code. *Automatic* follows the VS Code display language (German, otherwise English). Texts in the VS Code settings and command names always follow the VS Code display language.
config.language.enum0: Automatic (like the VS Code display language)
config.assignmentOperator: How assignments are shown in the structogram: *as written*, always as `:=` or always as `<-` (shown as `←` with *pretty operators*). Changes only the display (also in image exports), not the file; both notations are valid.
